_why: Status here is verified by `npm run gate`, not asserted by hand. A finding marked `fixed` must name either `checkedBy` (a static check id the gate already runs) or `verify` (a quote-free command the gate executes). If that check starts failing, the gate fails and this table is proven wrong — the entry cannot go quietly stale.

findings.title: serve bound every interface with auth off (RCE via npm postinstall)
Unauthenticated build API rendered any absolute local path
Attribute injection / XSS: escapeHtml did not escape quotes
Subdomain `..` escaped the hosting dir; CLI --name was never slugified
findings.detail: The server-side slug guard landed in v3.7.0 (checkedBy inv-6). The CLI deploy path (index.ts) still passes args.name through raw when no --org is set, so `brewdocs deploy --name ../x` writes outside the hosting dir. Closing this means routing that path through deploy.ts's deriveSubdomain/combineSubdomain.

findings.title: emitRedirects writes outside outDir via a `from: "../x"` key
findings.detail: Reachable from any repo's brewdocs.yml (`redirects:`). The `skip: file exists` guard prevents overwriting but not creating outside the output tree. emitAliasPages also does not sanitize its target.
findings.fixHint: aliases.ts: treat both `from` and the alias target as site-root-relative, resolve, and reject anything not under outDir.

findings.title: publish.yml publishes on any v* tag with no typecheck or smoke build
findings.detail: ci.yml runs typecheck + smoke build; publish.yml runs only `npm ci` + `npm test`. A tag on a commit whose types do not compile still publishes three packages. `npm run verify` now exists and is the honest gate to call here.
findings.fixHint: publish.yml: call `npm run verify` (or add the typecheck + smoke steps) before the three npm publish steps.

findings.title: @brewdocs/core ships raw TypeScript; plain Node cannot import it
findings.detail: 55 .ts files, no dist in `files`, no exports map pointing at JS. `import '@brewdocs/core'` under plain Node throws ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING; it works only under tsx. The repo's own alias works because the workspace symlink resolves outside node_modules.
findings.fixHint: Ship dist/ (remove it from .gitignore for the package, or build in prepublishOnly), add files: [dist], and an exports map with types. Read decision D-2 first — it explains why main points at src today.

findings.title: API key scopes are stored and printed but never enforced
findings.detail: keys.ts persists `scopes`, `keys list` displays them, tests assert them — but server.ts contains no reference to scopes. A `--scope build` key performs every operation.
findings.fixHint: Return the validated ApiKeyRecord from authenticate() instead of a boolean, then check the required scope per route. Or delete scopes and the flag so the surface stops advertising a boundary it does not have.

findings.title: Rate limiter trusts X-Forwarded-For unconditionally
findings.detail: Spoofing a new header value per request defeats the limiter, which is the only brake on the (network-touching, expensive) /api/build path.
findings.fixHint: Only honour X-Forwarded-For behind an explicit --trust-proxy flag / known proxy list; otherwise key on req.socket.remoteAddress.

findings.title: Analytics/registry endpoints leak when keys exist but no admin token is set
findings.detail: needsAuth is driven by the token, not by whether keys are configured. With keys present and BREWDOCS_TOKEN unset, /api/stats, /api/sites and /api/registry answer unauthenticated. The trust-boundary table in PROJECT_MAP.md shows these three as guards=**none**.
findings.fixHint: Require a key for the read endpoints too when keys are configured, or gate them behind a `read` scope (which pairs with finding #9).

findings.title: Theme slot partials resolve relative to the manifest (arbitrary file read)
findings.detail: A themes/brand.yml committed by a repo owner can name a slot value like ../../id_rsa; manifestSlots() reads it and the build can embed it in a published page.
findings.fixHint: theme-manifest.ts: resolve the partial against the source root and reject paths outside it — the same boundary-aware pattern as INV-3/INV-5.

findings.title: Pages workflow uses npm install instead of npm ci
findings.detail: .github/workflows/brewdocs.yml runs `npm install` on a tree that contains package.json scripts, with pages: write + id-token: write granted.

findings.title: Doc/reality drift (test counts, root package version, gitignored roadmap)
findings.detail: Test counts, file/LOC totals and the HTTP surface table are now parsed by scripts/map.mjs instead of typed, and CI fails when the map is stale. Remaining sub-items are cosmetic: root package.json still says 0.1.0 while all three workspaces publish 3.7.0, and ROADMAP.md is still gitignored.

findings.title: python adapter executes a bundled helper against the target tree
findings.detail: Bounded by a 60s timeout and 32MB buffer but unsandboxed. Acceptable for a chosen local build; must not run for a remote source without a warning.
findings.fixHint: Warn (or refuse) when the python adapter is the one that fires for a source that was fetched rather than a local path.

findings.title: No CSRF/Origin check on write endpoints
findings.detail: Any web page can POST to an open instance on the user's LAN with a simple request (no preflight when content-type is text/plain).
findings.fixHint: Reject cross-site Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site on POST endpoints.

findings.title: No golden-output test for the renderer
findings.detail: A 958-line renderer that emits its own JS has no snapshot test — which is why the attribute-injection bug survived 311 green tests.
findings.fixHint: Add a snapshot test over the example gallery's built HTML. The fuzz suite already builds every example, so the fixture is free.

findings.title: api.test.ts was flaky under load (2 tests at a 30s timeout)
findings.detail: A full-suite run on 2026-09-26 failed two endpoint tests at 31.2s / 33.9s against `{ timeout: 30_000 }`; a solo run of the file passed in 28.7s and an immediate re-run of the full suite went green. Both tests do a full TS extraction synchronously, so they are sensitive to load. Found by running the suite while building the map generator.
